subject: Recap + next steps: long-context evaluation for clinical summarization
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acmehealth.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@meditech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: long-context evaluation for clinical summarization

Hi Samira / Luis — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can set up an evaluation that answers your main concerns.

What I heard you say:
- Primary goal: convert multi-page clinical encounter notes into concise, reliable summaries for downstream consumption (triage, coding).
- Typical doc characteristics: mean ~40k tokens, spikes up to ~95k tokens; lots of structured sections and repeated templated text.
- Key risks: truncation of important context (especially discharge instructions and recent medication changes), hallucinations around medication changes, and strict audit requirements (PII handling + audit logs).
- Latency & throughput targets: interactive latency preferred <2s for short summaries, batch summarization OK up to ~10s per doc for nightly runs.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Long-context model variants: our long-window family (redwood-long-64k, redwood-long-128k) and fallbacks optimized for throughput (redwood-32k). We can run these as hosted trials or on Dedicated capacity depending on isolation/SLA needs.
- Truncation strategy: configurable windowing + sliding-window + hierarchical summarization to preserve head/tail context; we can surface where text was truncated and offer automatic secondary passes focused on tail sections.
- Eval plan: run an initial 2-week PoC using a representative prompt set (attached draft) and a small sample of redacted notes you provide. We'll measure ROUGE/BERTScore, entity F1 for medications/dosage/events, and a manual hallucination spot-check.
- Security: support for Private deployment / VPC and KMS integration for keys; detailed audit logs are available for inference requests.

Attached for your review: prompt_set_acme_clinical_v1.txt (draft prompt + examples) and a short summary of a Redwood internal long-context benchmark (long_context_eval_summary.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a small redacted sample set (5–10 notes) — can be zipped — we will not store PII and can run in an isolated tenant.
2) Redwood runs a targeted evaluation and returns a short report + sample outputs within 5 business days.
3) Technical deep dive with Karthik (SE) to discuss model selection, quantization options, and deployment mode (hosted vs Dedicated).

Can you confirm you’re comfortable sharing a redacted sample and whether Acme prefers Hosted trial or an isolated Dedicated trial? If helpful I can schedule the technical deep dive for next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: long-context evaluation for clinical summarization

Thanks Marissa — good recap and helpful to see the prompt draft. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Sample sizes: mean ~40k tokens is right; the 95k is an outlier (rare but critical). We need to understand exactly how tail truncation is handled because important medication changes are often at the end.
- Sliding-window: would that re-run inference over overlapping windows and stitch outputs? How do you avoid duplication or contradiction across windows?
- PII constraints: we can share fully redacted notes or a synthetic dataset. Can you confirm Redwood’s retention policy for trial runs and whether logs are encrypted at rest?
- Evaluation metrics: entity F1 for medications is the most important to our clinicians; automated ROUGE and BERTScore can be noisy. We’d like to include a clinician-rated fidelity score too.

I’ve attached a small sample bundle (acme_sample_patient_notes.zip) with internal IDs — the data team will redact identifiers before sending more.

We prefer an isolated Dedicated trial if possible, at least for the initial eval.

—Samira
Director of Clinical Informatics
Acme Health
samira@acmehealth.com

Samira — thanks for the sample and the great questions. I wanted to answer the technical bits and outline what we’ll run during the PoC.

1) Truncation & sliding-window stitching
- Approach: we do a two-pass strategy by default. First pass: a long-window model (redwood-long-128k if trial infra allows) ingests the full document and emits a candidate summary with per-token provenance tags. If the doc exceeds a single-window limit, we fall back to an overlapping-window pass: windows overlap by ~25% and we use a simple reconciliation policy (ranked by provenance score + clinician-defined anchors) to deduplicate and stitch.
- Avoiding contradictions: we surface candidate spans that conflict and either (a) run a micro-aggregation pass focused on the conflict spans, or (b) return both candidates and a confidence score so a downstream rule can pick. For clinical notes we recommend the micro-aggregation pass with a focused prompt that asks the model to reconcile medication lists and recent changes.

2) Latency/throughput tradeoffs and model recommendations
- If you need interactive sub-2s latency on short queries, use redwood-32k (fast, lower memory); for the nightly/high-fidelity batch runs we recommend redwood-long-128k (higher compute, preserves context).
- Quantization: we can run the long models in int8 or int4 with small quality deltas for your tasks; we’ll include quantized vs fp16 comparisons in the report.

3) Evaluation plan we’ll run during the 2-week PoC
- Data: your redacted 5–10 notes + a synthetic augmentation set we generate to hit the 95k tail cases.
- Metrics: Rouge-L, BERTScore, medication-entity F1 (span-based), hallucination rate (manual sampling), and a small clinician fidelity rubric (1–5).
- Deliverables: a Jupyter notebook with eval code (redwood_eval_notebook.ipynb), a short PDF report with example outputs and failure modes, and the annotated outputs so clinicians can review.

4) Security/retention
- Trial retention: by default we use isolated tenant storage for PoCs and purge raw inputs after 30 days unless you request otherwise. All logs encrypted at rest using KMS, and access is restricted to engineers on the PoC team. If you want a Private deployment we can provide an air-gapped option and HSM-backed key management.

Next logistic steps:
- Marissa will send a trial agreement and a short SOW. We can run the PoC in your Dedicated pool — we’ll provision a sandbox cluster and provide credentials for audit.
- Proposed scheduling: technical deep dive with me next Tuesday at 10am PT (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm).

I’ll kick off the eval once we have the redacted bundle and the signed PoC SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
